title: skills(objectstack-formula): "every predicate reads a record total over declared fields" contradicts the canonical sparse action-binding rule (declared-fields.ts, #4953), so agents drop the has() guard a list-row action needs
body:
domain:devx#2 · marchtian · session_017ihL2gLghEqeDKTbDTC7Zd

Filing gate: ① a named contradiction between a shipped skill and the code's canonical rule. Found while landing #28960, whose PR #29088 first removed a page's `has()` guard to match the skill. The seat put the guard back until this is settled.
Reader: `domain:skills` (`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`). Which side is canonical is a design call, so this goes to the maintainer before any edit.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "has() sparse action visible" → #28542 (open, cloud invitations page: Copy Invite Link hides on every row because the list does not project `expires_at`, which is live evidence of the sparse face), #28960 (open, the docs page). "has() is NOT a null check" → #28960 only. None names the contradiction.
reach: every coding agent that installs the bundled skills and writes an action `visible` / `disabled` predicate for a `list_item` location.
type: Bug

Business reason: the skill is the instruction an agent follows. It tells the agent `has()` is meaningless on any `record` binding. The code's own canonical rule says the action binding on a list row is sparse by decision and must be guarded with `has()`. An agent that follows the skill writes a list-row predicate that faults on an unprojected column, and the button hides silently, as #28542 shows.

## The two statements (read on `main` 2026-11-02)

- `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` § "`has()` is NOT a null check" (about lines 92–104): "Every predicate reads a `record` … that is **total over the object's declared fields** … So `has(record.<declared_field>)` … [is] uniformly `true` and tell[s] you nothing at all."
- `packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts` (about lines 28–45): "One binding is still sparse, and by decision rather than by gap: objectui's action `visible` / `disabled` binds whatever record the client already fetched — a record-detail read, or a LIST ROW carrying only the view's `$select` projection. That one is a DECISION (#4953 item 2) … **`has(record.x) && record.x != null`** … This doc comment is the CANONICAL statement of that rule."

Pages and examples follow one side or the other: `content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx` (about lines 113–117), `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx` (about line 615), `examples/app-crm/src/actions/convert-lead.action.ts` with `examples/app-crm/test/action-predicate-sparse-face.test.ts`, and `examples/app-showcase` (`src/ui/actions/index.ts`, `src/ui/pages/task-detail.page.ts`) follow the objectql rule. #29088's page now keeps the guard too.

Counter-evidence to measure: the #28960 dev read that list, grid and related-list views fetch every column an action predicate reads (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/predicate-fields.ts`, about lines 278 and 298). Kanban, calendar and gallery were not checked. If every face now fetches predicate columns, the objectql comment is the stale side.

## Wanted

- A ruling on which statement is canonical, after measuring every view face that binds an action predicate.
- Then one PR on the losing side: either the skill gains the action-binding exception (a skills edit, so it owes the full review), or `declared-fields.ts`, the CRM test and the pages drop the sparse rule.
